title: Remote delivery of problem management plus by nonclinicians for adults with psychological distress in New York City: A pilot feasibility study.
abstract: A single-arm trial was conducted to assess the feasibility, acceptability, and perceived utility of remotely delivered Problem Management Plus (PM+) in New York City. Two settings were used to evaluate these parameters: a graduate psychology training clinic and community-based organizations (CBOs) with staff without clinical training. Participants (= 45) received five sessions of PM+ delivered via Zoom. Primary clinical outcomes were distress related to client-generated problems (Psychological Outcomes Profile), depression symptoms (Patient Health Questionnaire-9), and anxiety symptoms (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7) administered at baseline and 1 week postintervention. Semistructured interviews were conducted with a subsample of participants and providers. Twenty-four helpers were trained in PM+: 15 students from the university training clinic and nine staff from two CBOs. Twenty-seven clients received PM+ from graduate students, and 18 clients received PM+ from CBO staff. Most clients (92.6% university clinic, 88.9% CBOs) completed all five PM+ sessions. Change from baseline to end line showed a medium to large effect across primary outcome measures in both settings. Qualitative interviews further supported the feasibility and acceptability of remote PM+. Remotely delivered PM+ appears to be feasible, acceptable, and safe, which supports its potential to expand the mental health workforce. Additional research is warranted to evaluate the effectiveness of remotely delivered PM+. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).
